thread.title: Sony Corporation ( SNE ) has been stuck in a time warp. In 2

author: Beulah Meriam K
title: Sony Corporation ( SNE ) has been stuck in a time warp. In 2
text:
Sony Corporation ( SNE ) has been stuck in a time warp. In 2008, Sony made 8,295 billion yen in revenue, and the company has forecasted 8,500 billion yen in revenue for fiscal 2018. Its earnings power still remains where it was 10 years ago. It is not that Sony didn’t do anything during this period; the problem for Sony is there are parts of the business that have outperformed, but there were also parts of businesses that seriously underperformed, and Sony got stuck in that rut. 
Source: Sony Investor Relations 
The first half-yearly report for the current fiscal from Sony is a very clear indicator of what will work for the company in the future and what will not. Sony’s Mobile Communications unit has been a persistent headache for the company. Though Sony’s mobile division did better than what it did last year, the real reason for the uptick was a favorable impact from forex. Despite that tailwind, operating income decreased from 4.2 billion yen last year to 1.2 billion yen this year, with a +0.2% forex impact.
What's Happening with Smartphones? The smartphone market is still growing, but a major portion of that growth is coming from emerging markets where low-cost Android phones rule the roost. The competition is extremely intense, and if you move up the ladder, you have iPhone and Samsung ( OTC:SSNLF ) sitting in complete control.
In Q1 2017, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) took home 83% of the smartphone industry’s profit share, while Samsung took home a 12.9% share. Together, Apple and Samsung accounted for just 37.7% of total unit share but walked away with nearly 96% of the industry’s profits.
